findings.summary: EventSub chat messages contain badges and Twitch says to inspect badges on each message rather than store them, because badges can change at any time.
findings.impact: Resolve moderator/VIP/subscriber only from the current message; do not cache these roles across messages.

findings.summary: Channel Chat Message includes target-channel badges and separate optional source_badges for Shared Chat; badge set IDs are values such as subscriber and metadata is not a role hierarchy.
findings.impact: Trust target-channel `badges` only; never grant role from `source_badges`. Product ordering is application policy, not a Twitch hierarchy.

findings.summary: GET /helix/channels/followers supports broadcaster_id and optional user_id. It requires a user access token with moderator:read:followers and the token user must be the broadcaster or a moderator. An empty data array can mean not-following, missing scope, or missing authorization.
findings.impact: Use configured broadcaster ID and current event user ID; verify token identity and scope before interpreting an empty array; unknown/error fails closed.

findings.summary: channel.follow v2 notifies when a new follow occurs and requires moderator:read:followers; it is not a current follower-membership snapshot and does not report unfollows.
findings.impact: Do not use EventSub follow notifications as authorization state or persist a follower cache.

findings.summary: Twitch validation returns client_id, user_id and scopes; third-party apps with OAuth sessions must validate at startup and hourly.
findings.impact: Check the broadcaster/client identity and granted follower scope; preserve existing hourly token validation. API/token failures are distinct from a confirmed non-follower.

findings.summary: Twitch requires apps to request only scopes needed for app functionality and documents scopes as user-authorized capabilities.
findings.impact: Request moderator:read:followers only after the streamer enables a follower threshold; do not add it to every installation unconditionally.

findings.summary: Twitch applies token-bucket limits; user-token API rate limits are per client ID and user per minute and responses expose rate-limit headers. 429 responses should use Ratelimit-Reset to determine when the bucket resets.
findings.impact: Call Helix only for parsed commands/help that need follower proof; do not retry aggressively; rate-limit or API failure must not authorize the action.

findings.summary: Twurple API 8.2.0 documents getChannelFollowers(broadcaster, user, pagination), which can check one user, and uses the broadcaster token by default.
findings.impact: Use the existing API client/adapter; no new SDK or raw HTTP integration is needed.

findings.summary: Twurple RefreshingAuthProvider 8.2.0 exposes getCurrentScopesForUser and scope-aware getAccessTokenForUser; refresh callbacks provide updated scopes.
findings.impact: Check currently available scopes before follower lookup and continue persisting every refresh atomically.

findings.summary: Twurple 8.2.0 exposes `badges` as Record<string,string> and `sourceBadges` separately; badge keys are set IDs.
findings.impact: Use the installed current SDK shape; keep regression tests for object-map and normalized array shapes.

codebaseEvidence: apps/api/src/commands/catalog.mjs stores explicit defaultRoles/immutableRoles and resolves OR allowlists.
apps/api/src/commands/authorization.mjs reads current broadcaster identity and badges; Twurple EventSub object maps are supported.
apps/api/src/twitch/eventsub-runtime.mjs forwards only target source channel and current badges; foreign Shared Chat events are rejected.
apps/api/src/twitch/oauth.mjs and apps/api/src/twitch/auth-runtime.mjs hard-code the current three required scopes.
apps/api/src/twitch/integration.mjs creates a single-channel broadcaster OAuth/API runtime and uses the existing Twitch adapter.
apps/api/src/persistence/queue-repository.mjs stores command policy as a versioned JSON Setting with explicit role arrays.
apps/api/src/http/queue-routes.mjs and apps/web expose protected catalog and policy editing; localization roots are provided by FND-8 catalogs.
unverifiedClaims: The product hierarchy (everyone < follower < subscriber < VIP < moderator < streamer) is an owner-approved application policy, not a Twitch-defined ranking.
No live Twitch follower lookup or scope authorization was performed during planning; SDK documentation and installed declarations only were verified.
dateAndVersionNote: Official Twitch and Twurple documentation was consulted on 2026-10-07. The repository currently pins all three Twurple packages to 8.2.0. Recheck docs and declarations before implementation if the lockfile changes.
